_readme: A1'S OWN DAILY RETAIL SENTIMENT, read off their free 'Retail Sent. History'
page. This is the ORACLE the Crowd column is validated against. It is not a
transcription of a screenshot: each series was read out of the rendered
chart's own accessible data table, with the dates taken from that same
chart's x-axis labels, so a value and its date come from one element pair.
WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE SNAPSHOT PAGE. The sibling 'Retail Sentiment'
page shows one bar per symbol for the latest available row, which is enough
to read A1's Bearish/Bullish/Neutral banding off but cannot be joined to a
Top Setups capture from a past date. This page can: it publishes a value per
symbol PER DAY, so a crowd cell captured on 2026-08-24 can be checked
against the long share A1 themselves recorded on 2026-08-24.
IT IS EVIDENCE, NOT A FEED. Nothing in this repo fetches these pages at
runtime and nothing should: they are embedded Looker Studio reports over A1's
proprietary 'EdgeFinder Pro' data, with no documented API. The standing rule
is no scraping and no undocumented endpoint as a production dependency.

source.method: Per symbol: set the report's Asset control, then read the 'RetailSentiment Long' column out of the chart's own <table> data representation and pair it index-for-index with the date labels rendered on the same chart's axis. Both series come from the chart element itself; neither was estimated from pixels.
source.attribution: Chart footer reads 'Source: A1 EdgeFinder Pro | www.a1trading.com'. No upstream provider is named on any A1 page.
source.coverage: Major pairs, minor pairs (crosses), metals, indices and commodities. NO currency-index rows -- searching the Asset control for 'POUND' returns nothing, so GB-POUND and its siblings exist only on the snapshot page. That is why the index rule has to be derived from the dollar pair rather than read directly.

_seriesNote: Long share of open retail positions, percent, quoted ON THE PAIR AS NAMED.
FX rows are whole integers; CFD rows (metals, indices) carry two decimals.
Only the tail of each series is recorded -- the dates this repo holds A1 Top
Setups cells for, plus enough surrounding days to show the trend is not a
single noisy print. EURUSD/GBPUSD/EURCHF/GBPCHF for 08-21..08-25 were already
on file from the previous round and are repeated here unchanged; re-reading
_snapshotIsNotThisSeries: The snapshot page and this history page do NOT agree on the same day, and
the difference is recorded rather than reconciled away. On 2026-08-30 the
snapshot read EURUSD 47, USDCHF 61 and GOLD 10.84; this history's last point
for those symbols is 2026-08-28 at 32, 69 and 58.13. NZDUSD is the one symbol
with a 2026-08-29 point here, and it reads 48 -- exactly the snapshot's NZDUSD.
So the snapshot is each symbol's LATEST row and the history simply lags for
some symbols, OR the two are populated by different jobs. Either way: join a
Top Setups capture to THIS file, never to the snapshot, and do not date the
snapshot's numbers by the day they were read.

topSetupsJoin._note: The section-1E validation. Every (symbol, date) where this repo holds BOTH an A1 Top Setups crowd cell and an A1 long share for the same date. Date-scoped: no row mixes 08-24 with 08-25. `via` names which resolution rung produced the long share.
topSetupsJoin._result: 8 of 8. The set is not trivially easy: it spans two capture dates, two majors, one CROSS (which has no futures contract and which a differenced model gets wrong), two METALS, and three CURRENCY INDICES -- two of them reached only through the derived dollar-pair rule, one of those inverted. The 40/60 bands and the per-symbol architecture reproduce every one.
topSetupsJoin._whatItDoesNotShow: It does not identify A1's upstream provider, and it does not show that a bought feed would agree with A1 to the point. It shows that GIVEN A1's own long share, the transformation in `lib/scoring/crowd.ts` returns A1's own cell.

_metalsCorrection.claim: A previous round recorded that 'metals, indices and commodities use a put/call ratio instead' of retail sentiment, inferred from the two-decimal formatting of those rows.
_metalsCorrection.finding: The formatting split is real but the conclusion was not. GOLD and SILVER appear in this same Retail Sentiment dataset with per-day long shares, and on 2026-08-24 those shares (95.08 and 91.05) score -1 under the unchanged 40/60 rule -- which is exactly A1's XAUUSD and XAGUSD crowd cell for that date. The demo does carry a separate 'Put-Call Ratio' page, so a put/call series exists; it is not what the Crowd column reads for metals.
_metalsCorrection.consequence: None for production today. Those two cells already resolve correctly from their own CFTC contracts, so nothing changes; but a retail feed keyed on metals would now be expected to agree rather than to break them.
